## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization on the streaming walk combined with a fused scatter to the framebuffer can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 9.198 ns/p at N=4000 to 6.396 at N=65000 — overhead amortization with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈61680). Cost stays FLAT at 6.378 through N=262000, then RISES modestly to 6.941 at N=4000000. The L1d spill at N≈963 lies below the first measured point. Death rate raises the floor without altering the N-shape: from ~6.4 ns/p at q=0.01 to ~13.6 at q=0.5, with the same flat-then-slight-rise profile throughout.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 10.66 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 42% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Bandwidth-bound but far from ceiling at low churn; transitions to overhead-bound as death rate rises, falling to 6.82 GB/s (27%) at q=0.25 and 4.98 GB/s (20%) at q=0.5. The transition is driven by death rate, not N: within each series bandwidth is nearly flat across N, confirming per-particle scatter/respawn cost as the bottleneck.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized walk1: `fmul.4s` and `fadd.4s` on four single-precision lanes, `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` for the remaining pair, across components of one particle (AoS stride 0x44=68). `ext.16b` and `mov.s v17[3]` rearrange components; `ld1.s {v16}[1]` is an indexed single-element gather. Walk2 (fused scatter) is entirely scalar: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` for byte-granular framebuffer writes, 18 `csel` for 0–255 clamping. The byte-store scatter explains the 42% ceiling cap; branchy respawn (`cmp`, `b`, `bl spawn`) drives death-rate sensitivity.

## Verdict
Partially — autovec occurred and the algo is bandwidth-bound at q≤0.05, but peak 10.66 GB/s is only 42% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes and branchy respawn cap bandwidth at 42% and collapse it to 20% by q=0.5 (4.98 GB/s). The hypothesis holds only weakly: no cache-spill knee appears, but the streaming-ceiling claim fails.
